questions.q: What is a Fabric pipeline built from?
options: Activities connected in a visual canvas — the same orchestration shape as Azure Data Factory
Only PySpark code, with no visual component at all
A single, non-configurable Copy activity
@dlt.table decorators, exactly like Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines
questions.explain: Fabric's pipelines aren't a new invention — they're the same ADF pipeline model, inside Fabric's workspace.

questions.q: What does a Copy activity actually do?
options: Moves data between a source and a destination, with no PySpark or SQL written at all
Transforms data using PySpark transformations
Trains a machine learning model on the copied data
Applies row-level security to the copied data
questions.explain: This mirrors the same movement-focused job Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 56 described ADF doing.

questions.q: Why does a Copy activity typically get chained with a separate notebook activity?
options: Copy activity moves bytes; the actual transformation logic runs separately in a Notebook activity, chained after it finishes
Notebook activities always run before Copy activities, never after
Copy activities can perform transformations just as well as notebooks, so chaining is unnecessary
Notebook activities cannot be used within a Fabric pipeline at all
questions.explain: This is the same movement-then-transformation split covered in the ADF-vs-Lakeflow comparison from the previous course.

questions.q: How does chaining a Notebook activity after a Copy activity in Fabric compare to Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 54?
options: It's the same idea as chaining a Lakeflow Job's Pipeline task after a notebook task — just the task types swapped in order and name
There's no comparable pattern in the Databricks & Delta Lake course
Fabric pipelines cannot chain multiple activity types together
Lesson 54's pattern only applies to real-time streaming, not batch pipelines
questions.explain: Both patterns chain a data-movement step with a transformation step, using each platform's own task/activity types.

questions.q: What does scheduling a Fabric pipeline correspond to, from the previous course?
options: The same underlying concept as Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 11's job schedule, just named a "trigger" and configured in Fabric's own UI
A completely new scheduling concept unrelated to anything in Databricks
Fabric pipelines cannot be scheduled at all, only run manually
Scheduling only applies to Notebook activities, never Copy activities
questions.explain: The underlying idea — running on a schedule — transfers directly, just under different terminology.
